assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework, with nominal rigidities, Calvo pricing, interest-rate rules and the optimizing-agent theory of monetary policy, is the core of how central banks think and model. Its influence on theory and on policy practice is very large and well confirmed.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread across many people. Calvo supplied the staggered-pricing device, Taylor the policy rule and the empirical policy-evaluation tradition, and Woodford the systematic microfounded synthesis for welfare-based policy analysis. Gali, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets have strong claims through estimation and the medium-scale DSGE models, so any three-person selection is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature. The key contributions date from the 1980s to the early 2000s and have been tested through several crises and policy regimes.
uncertainties: Which three of the eight credited names best capture the core contribution
Overlap with the 2022 prize on banking and the 2022 laureate Bernanke's work on monetary policy
Debate over whether the post-2008 and post-2020 performance of DSGE models weakens the case

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Collateral constraints, credit cycles and the financial accelerator explain how small shocks are amplified through balance sheets. The Kiyotaki–Moore mechanism and the Bernanke–Gertler accelerator are standard tools in macro-finance and in policy analysis after 2008.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore are the clear originators of the collateral-based credit-cycle model. Gertler is central to the financial accelerator and its quantitative implementation. Gilchrist is a significant empirical contributor but a less natural choice for a trio.
assessment.maturity: Mature. The foundational papers date from the late 1980s and the 1990s, and the framework has been extended and empirically supported across several crises.
uncertainties: Partial overlap with the 2022 prize for Bernanke, Diamond and Dybvig on banks and financial crises
Gertler also appears under the New Keynesian candidate, creating a possible double-counting issue
Empirical identification of amplification magnitudes remains debated

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structural estimation of differentiated-product demand (BLP) and of dynamic industry models changed empirical industrial organization. It is now routinely used in merger review, antitrust and regulation, and it spread to trade, health and public economics.
assessment.attribution: The BLP demand-estimation approach is clearly attributable to Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes. Pakes also has distinct dynamic-games and Ericson–Pakes contributions. Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin are important but are not the core of the BLP method.
assessment.maturity: Very mature. BLP dates from 1995 and the method has had decades of use, replication and refinement.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would prefer a broader empirical-IO prize that includes Bresnahan
Debates about identification and about the credibility of structural versus reduced-form approaches

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The work on skill-biased technological change, the task framework, and the labour-market effects of import competition reshaped how economists and policymakers understand wage inequality and the distributional effects of technology and trade. It combines theory-informed empirics with strong policy influence.
assessment.attribution: Autor is the common thread across the task approach and the China-shock work. Hanson is central to the trade-shock evidence, and Katz is central to the long-run demand-and-supply-of-skills literature. Dorn is a key co-author on the China shock but more junior. Acemoglu, a 2024 laureate, also contributed to the task and technology literature, which complicates attribution.
assessment.maturity: Fairly mature. The central papers date from the early 2000s to 2013 and have been confirmed, though they have also been refined and partly challenged.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2024 laureate Acemoglu's work on technology
Debate over the size and persistence of the China shock effects
Whether the committee would prefer to split the trade and technology strands

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification provides a principled way to state what data can establish without strong assumptions. Manski's bounds approach and the moment-inequality inference developed by Tamer and others changed econometric theory and increased the credibility of applied work.
assessment.attribution: Manski is the clear originator of the approach. Tamer is central to its extension to econometric models, including games. Molinari has substantial inferential contributions and is another candidate, but a two-person award best reflects the core.
assessment.maturity: Mature in theory, with Manski's foundational work from the late 1980s and 1990s. Applied adoption is real but less pervasive than for design-based methods.
uncertainties: Applied uptake is narrower than the theoretical importance suggests
Whether the committee would favour methodological prizes over substantive ones at this point
Whether Molinari should be included

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm-heterogeneity trade theory explains who trades, why gains from trade operate through reallocation, and how this connects to the large micro-data evidence on exporters. It extends the Krugman prize on new trade theory and is a standard framework in international trade.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the central model. Helpman contributed key theoretical and empirical extensions, including Helpman–Melitz–Yeaple on exports versus FDI and the work with Redding. Redding is a strong contributor, but the three-person list is less clearly tied to a single core discovery. Helpman also appears under the trade-policy candidate.
assessment.maturity: Mature. Over twenty years of theory and empirics, with extensive confirmation and refinement.
uncertainties: Prior recognition of new trade theory in 2008 may reduce the marginal case
Helpman's appearance across two candidates raises a double-counting question
Quantitative debates about the size of gains from trade

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The alternating-offers bargaining model and its market versions give the canonical strategic foundation for bargaining and decentralized trade. They underpin work in matching and search markets, labour economics, industrial organization and political economy.
assessment.attribution: Rubinstein (1982) is the foundational contribution. Rubinstein–Wolinsky is the key market-bargaining extension. Binmore made important contributions to the strategic and axiomatic link, but is a secondary choice for a trio.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with four decades of use. The theoretical results are firmly established.
uncertainties: Rubinstein's work also spans decision theory and modelling methodology, so the prize rationale could be framed more broadly
Stahl and Ståhl-style antecedents, and the weight to place on empirical relevance of the sequential-offer model
Game theory has been recognized several times, which may lower the marginal priority

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The use of population administrative data to measure intergenerational mobility and its local causes opened a large empirical programme. It has had substantial policy impact on neighbourhoods and opportunity, and it shows the value of large-scale linked data in economics.
assessment.attribution: Chetty leads the programme and its data infrastructure. Hendren is central to the neighbourhood-effects and causal-place evidence. Friedman and Katz are major contributors, with Katz overlapping the Moving to Opportunity tradition and the labour-demand candidate. The credit structure is somewhat collective.
assessment.maturity: Moderately mature. The key papers are from about 2014 to 2022, and long-run replication and the confirmation of causal claims are still developing.
uncertainties: The work is relatively recent, so lasting influence is harder to judge
Credit is spread across a large collaborative team
Debate over the causal interpretation of place effects and over measurement of mobility across contexts
